chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man enters the mosque and he is not following his companion (the Imam), and there remains upon the Imam one verse or two verses, so he fears that if he were to recite the Adhan and Iqamah, the Imam would go into Ruku', then let him say: 'The Salat has been established! The Salat has been established! Allah is the Greatest! Allah is the Greatest! There is no god except Allah!', and let him enter into the Salat.

key_terms.آيَةٌ: A verse (referring to a portion of Quranic recitation)
key_terms.أَذَّنَ: To recite the Adhan (call to prayer)
key_terms.أَقَامَ: To recite the Iqamah (call to establish prayer)
key_terms.قَدْ قَامَتِ الصَّلَاةُ: The Salat has been established (part of Iqamah)

ai.seo_question: What should a person say if they enter the mosque late and fear the Imam will bow before they can join?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the practical flexibility (rukhas) in Shia jurisprudence, prioritizing the preservation of congregational unity (Jama'ah) over the ritual completeness of the call to prayer. It reflects the scholarly principle that the Iqamah serves primarily to signal the start of prayer for latecomers, allowing them to join the Imam without causing disruption or missing the Ruku'. This emphasizes the Shia emphasis on the spiritual and communal benefits of following the Imam over rigid adherence to procedural details when time is critical.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub, from Muawiya Bin Kaseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When the man enters the Masjid and he is not accomplishing it with his companions, and there remains upon the prayer-leader, either a Verse or two Verses, so he fears that if he were to recite an Azān and an Iqamah, he (the prayer-leader) would go into Rukū (a bowing), so let him say, ‘The Salāt has been established! Allahazwj is the Greatest! Allahazwj is the Greatest! There is no god except for Allahazwj!’, and let him enter into the Salāt’.
en.sarwar: 22. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ariy has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Ayyub from Mu’adh ibn Kathir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

A man may enter a Masjid and is not following his companion in Salah (prayer). He finds the Imam has only one verse to recite or two verses. He is afraid of not being able to join the Imam in Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees) if he says Adhan or ‘Iqamah. He can say, ‘Salah (prayer) has began, Salah (prayer) has began, Allah is great beyond description, Allah is great beyond description. No one deserves worship except Allah,’ he then can begin al-Salah (prayer).”’
